target_customer: Specialty and surgical practices (orthopaedics, ophthalmology, retina, rheumatology, skilled nursing)
problem: Prior authorization, eligibility checks and referral management consume practice staff time and delay patient care.
business_model: Per-authorization pricing with volume discounts, per the Irish Times
product_category: AI back office automation for patient access

founders.name: Aaron Cullen
founders.background_notes: Grew up in Dublin and moved to the US at 18 per the Irish Times.

founders.name: Jaylem Brar
founders.background_notes: Described as a software engineer; education not found.

competitors.name: Cohere Health
competitors.what: AI prior authorization platform mainly for health plans
competitors.funding_then: $90M Series C in May 2025, about $200M total

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires EHR-native integration, payer portal workflows, an AI call center and HIPAA compliance; heavy integration work more than research.

defensibility.rationale: Deep EHR integration and HIPAA compliance create friction for switching; the product is specialty-focused, but Cohere and others are well funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action aimed at Mendelia found.

market_need_then: Prior authorization is a known administrative burden and CMS tightened rules in 2025 and 2026; the Irish Times reports first paying customers and clinician referrals driving growth.

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and plain: 'Clear the path from patient to care'; 'The AI teammate for patient access'.

branding.brand_signature: Doughnut visits to clinics described as a go-to-market tactic in the Irish Times, not as official branding.
branding.community_and_virality: Irish Times feature (August 2026) and Built In listings; no merch or fan communities found. Searches are polluted by Mendel AI and Mendelian.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive coined name with a clear tagline, but it resembles Mendel AI and Mendelian and there is no brand-driven pull evidence.

outcome_analysis: Mendelia is a Winter 2026 YC company founded by two ex-Brellium colleagues, active with first paying customers and about six staff per the Irish Times in August 2026. Selling to surgical practices through clinician referrals is a promising wedge, with the founders' healthcare administration background as an edge. Funded prior authorization rivals make execution speed and integration depth the deciding factors.
notes: Round recorded as other: the Irish Times reports a $500,000 start-up capital from Y Combinator but gives no date, so the date is only 2026. The same article says the founders also raised pre-seed money with no investor or amount named. Funding is partial. Founding date 'last January' inferred as January 2026 from the article. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition. Undated competitors seen in searches (Anterior, Latitude Health) were omitted because no dated source was found.
